headline: Hot PPI couldn't buy the October hike back: wholesale prices ran +1.3% — the biggest jump since March 2022 — and the market still faded October to ~29%, because the AI risk-off owned the tape. The 10-year collapsed ~27bp off the CPI-day spike to a three-week low, the dollar fell against every G10 currency except the aussie, gold reclaimed ~$4,150+, and the franc — not the yen — was the haven that finally showed up. Warsh speaks 10:30pm CT, the last Fed voice before Saturday's blackout.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: Wholesale prices jumped 1.3% — more than double what was expected, the hottest since March 2022 — and the market shrugged: October hike odds fell to ~29%, the 10-year collapsed ~27bp, and the dollar faded to ~102.05.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: Wholesale prices — the factory-gate version of inflation — rose 1.3% in a month, the fastest since March 2022. Gasoline (+20.3%) did about half the work.
What happened: Expected 0.6%, printed 1.3% — more than double. Core 0.7% vs 0.3% expected. Thread: this morning said PPI was the next verdict after Bowman and Daly talked October down to ~31.6%. The verdict came back hot — and didn't matter.
What it means and why: Hot inflation should mean more Fed pressure → higher yields → stronger dollar. Instead the fear tape won: AI-debt stress sent money into Treasuries for safety, pushing yields DOWN — the 10-year fell ~27bp to a three-week low. October slipped to ~29%; December (~90%+) never blinked.
What it indicates for the dollar: Softer — the chain ran in reverse. DXY faded to ~102.05. The question to carry: when hot data meets fear, which tape is running the market?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Warsh speaks 10:30pm CT — the last Fed voice before Saturday's Oct 17 blackout (Hammack spoke 3:30pm CT; no verified readout had surfaced by NY close — her Monday 'rates need to move higher' stance is already priced). Friday 7:30am CT: import prices + housing starts; 8:15am CT: industrial production. September PCE lands Oct 29, after the meeting.

scenarios.base: October stays ~25-30% into the blackout; the meeting is priced as a hold and DXY chops 101.8-102.5.
scenarios.bear: A patient Warsh plus soft Friday data — October falls toward ~15% and DXY retests 101.5.
scenarios.bull: Warsh re-arms the hike — October back toward ~45% and DXY retests 102.75.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro rode the dollar fade to ~1.12 (+0.5%) even as its own data disappointed — eurozone factory output missed and France's inflation confirmed the energy overshoot.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The euro rose ~0.5% to ~1.1216, erasing the CPI-day selloff — on no good news of its own.
What happened: Eurozone factory output fell 0.5% (expected flat); France's September inflation confirmed at 3.4%, the highest since January 2024, energy-driven. Thread: this morning said the pair trades the Fed leg, not the ECB leg.
What it means and why: Neither print moved the pair — that's the tell. EUR/USD is a ratio: it rises when the dollar falls. The ECB leg is steady (Oct 29 hike ~12% priced); the dollar leg did all the work.
What it indicates for the euro: Higher, but on borrowed strength. Chain: US yields fell → dollar faded broadly → euro rode it up. The question to carry: which leg is moving the pair?
chapters.fx: What to watch: eurozone final CPI Friday 9am CT; US import prices + housing starts Friday 7:30am CT for the dollar leg; France's revenue-section vote Oct 20 and Moody's Oct 23.
numbers: France HICP 3.4% y/y final (highest since Jan 2024); ECB Oct 29 hike ~12%

scenarios.base: EUR/USD chops 1.115-1.125; the dollar leg decides, the ECB leg steadies.
scenarios.bear: A hawkish Warsh re-fires October — 1.115 retests and the record EUR shorts (-99,332) stay loaded.
scenarios.bull: Soft Friday US data — the record-shorts squeeze runs toward 1.13.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling rode the dollar fade to ~1.324 (+0.4%) as a Reuters poll showed 54 of 63 economists expect the November hike — while Pill said it 'need not be the start of a long series.'
chapters.meaning:
What this was: Sterling rose to ~1.324 as a Reuters poll locked in the November hike — 54 of 63 economists expect +25bp to 4.00%.
What happened: No majority expects another hike after November, though markets price four by Sep 2027. Pill said a hike 'need not be the start of a long series' — hawkish on inflation, dovish on the path. Thread: this morning said the GDP beat covered the growth leg while Pill capped 2027.
What it means and why: A hike supports a currency, but November is ~86% priced — it's the PATH that moves sterling now. The gap between 'one hike' (economists) and 'four' (markets) is where the next move lives.
What it indicates for the pound: Supported near-term, capped beyond. Chain: priced hike = no surprise = no new fuel. The question to carry: is the market pricing the hike or the path?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bailey Friday 2am CT (3rd of 4); UK retail sales Friday 1am CT; the Oct 28 budget; BoE decision Nov 5.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: USD/JPY faded to ~157.7 with the 10-year as Koeda warned against getting 'overly cautious' on hikes — but the franc, not the yen, was Thursday's haven.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The yen firmed as USD/JPY slipped to ~157.7 with the 10-year, while Koeda warned against getting 'overly cautious' on hikes.
What happened: Koeda put the neutral rate 'considerably above 1%.' October stays ~9%, December >80%. Thread: this morning said the BoJ is frozen in December-not-October and the haven bid isn't independent.
What it means and why: The yen has two engines — the rate gap (US yields down → gap narrows → yen up) and fear. Both pointed the same way, softly. The haven lesson: franc +0.59% beat yen +0.34% — financial fear (AI debt) bids Europe's haven over Japan's.
What it indicates for the yen: Mildly supportive on both engines. The question to carry: rate gap or fear — which is driving?
chapters.fx: What to watch: US import prices + housing starts Friday for the yield leg; BoJ Oct 29-30 — the forecasts decide whether machinery orders (+5.2% beat) or industrial output (-2.4%) matters.
numbers: USD/JPY ~157.6-157.9 (-0.2%; faded with the 10Y to its 3-wk low)
BoJ Oct 30 hike ~9%; December >80%; 160 is the intervention line

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The haven finally showed up: USD/CHF fell ~0.57% to ~0.83 — Thursday's best G10 move against the dollar — while soft Swiss PPI kept December cut risk on the table.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The franc woke up — USD/CHF fell ~0.57% to ~0.831, the best G10 move against the dollar.
What happened: The haven bid picked Europe over Japan (CHF/JPY +0.36%). Swiss PPI was soft (+0.3% vs 0.6% expected). Thread: this morning said the franc only moves on a verified shock or de-escalation — the shock was credit fear.
What it means and why: When fear is about credit and AI debt, the flow goes franc first, gold second, yen third. With rates pinned at 0.00%, the SNB can barely cut — and a central bank that can't cut is itself franc-supportive.
What it indicates for the franc: Bid into the weekend. Chain: credit fear → safety demand for francs → USD/CHF down. The question to carry: financial fear or geopolitical fear?
chapters.fx: What to watch: EUR/CHF as the contagion gauge; Trump's Saturday-evening Hormuz deadline; SNB Dec 10.
numbers: USD/CHF ~0.831 (-0.57% — best G10 vs the dollar Thursday)

scenarios.bear: Verified de-escalation — the fear premium clears and USD/CHF drifts back up.
scenarios.bull: A verified supply shock or a Saturday-deadline strike — the haven bid extends.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The aussie was the only G10 currency to fall against the dollar Thursday (-0.48% to ~0.694): a jobs miss plus a risk-off tape is the worst possible combination for a risk proxy.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The aussie fell ~0.5% to ~0.694 — the only G10 currency to lose against the dollar.
What happened: Jobs missed badly (-39.3K vs +20K expected); unemployment hit 4.7%, a five-year high above the RBA's 4.5% forecast. Thread: this morning said the miss broke the improving-AUD shape and pushed $0.70 further away.
What it means and why: The aussie is a risk proxy — it falls when the world feels scared. A jobs miss (less RBA hike pressure; November odds pared from ~33%) landing on a risk-off tape is the worst combo. Record shorts (-98,588) leave a squeeze loaded, but it needs soft US data plus an RBA willing to hike through slack.
What it indicates for the aussie: Pressured on both legs. Chain: weak jobs → less hike pressure → lower expected yields → less reason to hold AUD; plus risk-off selling. The question to carry: does the RBA hike through the slack or blink?
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBA's Kent speaks Saturday; China Q3 GDP Monday; US import prices + IP Friday; RBA Nov 2-3 is the verdict.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The tug-of-war's legs pushed the same way for once: the EIA confirmed a -8.6M-barrel draw and WTI rallied +2.7% while the dollar leg faded — the loonie firmed gently to ~1.42.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The loonie firmed gently to ~1.42 as oil rallied and the dollar faded — both legs of the tug-of-war pulling its way.
What happened: The EIA confirmed an 8.6M-barrel draw (vs +0.2M expected); WTI +2.7% to $96.42 while Brent sat ~$106.10 — the spread compressed to ~$9.7. Factory sales beat on prices, not volumes. Thread: this morning said 1.41-1.43 chop holds until one leg wins.
What it means and why: Canada sells oil, so tighter physical supply supports the loonie. The spread is the tell: the war premium lives in Brent as freight cost — compressing on shadow-fleet easing talk means the fear premium is leaking, and easing would hit Brent harder than WTI.
What it indicates for the loonie: Gently supportive. Chain: big draw → tighter oil → better Canadian terms of trade → CAD bid; plus dollar fade. 1.4299 is the line in the sand. The question to carry: which leg wins — the oil bid or the dollar?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Macklem speaks 11:15pm CT tonight; BoC's Alexopoulos Friday; Canada housing starts Friday 7:30am CT; US data Friday; a break of 1.4299 opens 1.44.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi drifted +0.2% to ~0.562 on the dollar fade while RBNZ's Conway confirmed the two-way bet: October 28 is 'wide open,' but the direction is 'most likely up.'
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The kiwi drifted +0.2% to ~0.562 on the dollar fade, still hovering above its 52-week low.
What happened: RBNZ's Conway called Oct 28 'wide open' — hold or hike — but said the direction is 'most likely up': oil gains plus a weaker NZD are adding near-term inflation pressure. Thread: this morning framed it as a two-way bet (~50% priced) with Oct 21 CPI as the settler.
What it means and why: A hawkish lean supports a currency (expected hikes → higher expected yields → inflows), but 'wide open' means nothing is priced — so the kiwi drifts instead of trending. Tonight's data is texture; CPI is the verdict.
What it indicates for the kiwi: Stuck near the lows until CPI decides. Chain: hot CPI → hike priced → NZD re-rates; soft CPI → hold → heavy. The question to carry: what does CPI say about October 28?

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: The EIA confirmed the draw (-8.6M barrels): WTI rallied +2.7% to $96.42 while Brent lagged — the spread compressed to ~$9.7 as the freight premium, not demand, is what's priced.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: The EIA confirmed the huge draw (-8.6M barrels) — WTI rallied 2.7% to $96.42 while Brent didn't follow.
What happened: Crude -8.6M vs +0.2M expected, 3% below the five-year average. Brent sat ~$106.10; the spread compressed to ~$9.7. Thread: this morning said $104-108 holds until a verified shock or ceasefire, and the EIA was the confirmation test.
What it means and why: A draw is physical tightness — bullish. But Brent lagging says the war premium is freight cost leaking out on shadow-fleet easing talk (a consideration, not an action). Iran sanctions and MOAB planning kept the escalatory lane open. The spread is the gauge: toward $15 = Hormuz risk back; toward $5 = premium gone.
What it indicates for oil: Range intact — tightness re-bid WTI without breaking $104-108. The question to carry: is the spread pricing shipping risk or demand?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Trump's Saturday-evening Hormuz deadline; any US/CENTCOM response; whether shadow-fleet easing talk becomes action; spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: The anti-dollar bid re-armed: gold ran to ~$4,150-4,175 (+1.5%+, futures $4,181 +1.8%) as the rate leg collapsed — the haven that works when FX havens hesitate.
chapters.meaning:
What this was: Gold rallied to ~$4,150-4,175 (futures +1.8% to $4,181) as the rate leg collapsed.
What happened: Hot CPI had knocked it down 1.7% yesterday to $4,107.90; today's three-week low in the 10-year flipped it. Thread: this morning called it the both-engines moment.
What it means and why: Gold runs on two engines — real yields (gold pays nothing, so falling yields make it cheaper to hold) and fear (AI-debt stress, ~$1B in crypto liquidations). Both fired. Gold +1.8% vs franc +0.59% vs yen +0.34%: the haven that works when FX havens hesitate.
What it indicates for gold: Re-armed but capped by the 10-year. Chain: yields down → gold's competition fades → gold up; fear up → haven demand → gold up. Soft Friday data opens $4,300; a hawkish Warsh sends it back toward $4,000. The question to carry: which engine is running — rates or fear?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Warsh 10:30pm CT; US import prices + housing starts + IP Friday; the 10-year (~5.05-5.10%) is the cap to watch.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100-4,175 under the rate cap; direction comes from Friday's data.
scenarios.bear: A hawkish Warsh re-fires October — real yields jump again and gold slides back toward $4,000.
scenarios.bull: Soft Friday data collapses the repricing — gold re-arms toward $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
